text:
nora: FYI - Solvexa reported a surprise $21,450 overage on their Dedicated July invoice (INV-2026-9933). They say it aligns exactly with the cross-region failover on 2026-07-18.
diego: I exported the billing aggregation windows. Looks like our billing cutoff window for dedicated pooling closes at 00:00UTC but the failover occurred at 23:58 local and some meters were attributed in both July and the August rollup because of a windowing race.
carla-finance: windowing race -> could cause same request to be counted in two billing cohorts. what's the scale?
suresh-ops: sample from aggregated meter stream (sanitized):

```
2026-07-18T23:58:09Z,Solvexa,eu-west,D-POOL-COMMIT,22000
2026-07-19T00:00:05Z,Solvexa,eu-west,D-POOL-COMMIT,21980
2026-07-19T00:00:06Z,Solvexa,eu-west,D-POOL-BURST,180000
```

suresh-ops: because the collector flush happens near the cutoff, some events were duplicated into both the July finalization and the August initial delta. Net duplicated commit-like units ~43,980.
carla-finance: at our amortized reserved-commit effective unit value that's roughly $14,500 of misattributed commit cost. Invoice overage is $21,450, so remaining $6,950 appears to be genuine burst during failover.
vendor-ops: we checked with MeterBridge (our metering vendor) and they confirmed their forwarder retried a partial flush during the cutoff window and re-emitted failed batches. Ticket MB-9021 opened, vendor accepts responsibility for duplicate emissions.
nora: customer is asking for the full reversal + SLA credit. They emphasised this impacted their budget planning for the month.
carla-finance: recommended plan: (1) reverse $14,500 misattributed commit charges (vendor-recoverable), (2) apply a discretionary SLA goodwill credit of $5,000 (non-recoverable) to acknowledge the service disruption, (3) leave $1,950 as validated burst that we can show in the reconciliation. Total provisional credit = $19,500.
diego: breakdown looks fair. please include the per-line accounting memos and tag with vendor ticket MB-9021.
carla-finance: provisional accounting entry to post now:

```
DR Revenue Adjustment 6102: $19,500.00
CR Accounts Receivable 1200: $19,500.00
```

carla-finance: vendor-recoverable portion GL will be tracked separately with tag VendorRecovery/MeterBridge/MB-9021. finance requests vendor admission and reimbursement plan before changing final GL.
vendor-ops: MeterBridge provided a signed statement and committed to reimbursement within 10 business days. They also exposed a patch to avoid partial flush retries at cutoff.
suresh-ops: ops will add a billing-cutoff guard that rejects duplicate batch IDs during finalization and a smoke test in the pre-cutoff pipeline.
nora: I'll send the customer note. draft: "We detected duplicated metering events that caused misattributed reserved capacity charges during your failover. We've issued a provisional credit of $19,500 while we reconcile with our metering vendor. We'll follow up with final settlement within 10 business days. Apologies for the disruption."
carla-finance: please attach the line-item CSV and the vendor ticket. Also, because credit > $10k, loop in legal for the communication language.
nora: looping legal now.
carla-finance: approvals needed: @carla-finance, @suresh-ops, @vendor-ops, @legal - react :thumbsup: to authorize provisional adjustment.
carla-finance: (reacts) :thumbsup:
suresh-ops: (reacts) :thumbsup:
vendor-ops: (reacts) :thumbsup:
billing-bot: Invoice INV-2026-9933 status updated -> ADJUSTED (credit $19,500.00) / VendorTicket: MB-9021
carla-finance: leave thread open until MeterBridge reimbursement posts and AR final reconciles. Action items: post provisional credit, attach reconciliation CSV, receive vendor reimbursement note, publish short RCA and remediation to affected customers.
